items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Small, clear one-line changes that fit the existing style, e.g. `self._fqdn = socket.getfqdn().encode('idna').decode('ascii')`. The inline IDNA conversion has no comment, which is a minor gap.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The same `.encode('idna').decode('ascii')` call is pasted into both utils.py get_fqdn and message.py `make_msgid(domain=str(DNS_NAME).encode('idna')...)`. There is no shared helper, and the second conversion is redundant once get_fqdn already converts.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: No errors are swallowed and there are no magic constants. IDNA failures (e.g. empty labels) raise instead of producing a bad Message-ID. The reference handles this the same way.

items.name: Conversion is encoding-independent and safe for ASCII names
items.name_zh: 转换与编码无关且不影响 ASCII 主机名
items.evidence: Conversion is applied at the source in get_fqdn for every encoding, and ASCII hosts pass through unchanged. But it is also repeated inline at the make_msgid call, so the domain is encoded twice (harmless, since encoding ASCII is a no-op) and the idna call is duplicated.
